newsitem.title: USA: Computerworld survey shows PC-maker satisfaction.
newsitem.headline: Computerworld survey shows PC-maker satisfaction.

text.p: Customer satisfaction with personal computer makers is up sharply in 1996, according to a Computerworld survey of 250 information managers.

An annual survey commissioned by Computerworld newspaper showed overall vendor satisfaction rose to 74 percent in 1996 from 60 percent in 1995. Hewlett-Packard Co and Dell Computer Corp earned the highest ratings for overall satisfaction.
Users rated the companies on such issues as quality, system performance and technical support. The survey targeted high-end, multimedia PCs typically used by the most demanding corporate users.
